types.name: Activity
types.description:
An `Activity` is a single sport event happening at a specific time.

  `Activities` can be individually bookable units (e.g. _Classes_) or part of a larger bookable `ActivityGroups` (e.g. _Courses_ or _Workshops_)

fields.name: bookable
fields.description:
Information on _whether_ and _how_ this `Activity` is bookable.

  If this field is `null` this `Activity` is _not_ bookable.
  This can have multiple reasons:
  - This `Activity` is not itself an individually _bookable unit_, but just a part of an `ActivityGroup` which has to be booked as a whole.
  - This `Activity` is _archived_ or _cancelled_
  - The `PublicationState` of its `ActivityGroup` is not `ACTIVE`

  If this field is _not_ `null` this `Activity` is generally bookable.
  Note that further restriction like a registration window or a limitation of spots can still apply.

fields.name: end
fields.description: The end of this `Activity` provided in the `DateOutput` format

fields.name: hasOnlineStream
fields.description: Whether this `Activity` has an online stream

fields.name: id
fields.description: The universally unique identifier for this `Activity`

fields.name: isArchived
fields.description:
Whether this `Activity` is _archived_.
  An `Activity` can be _archived_ if the `ActivityGroup` containing it was archived or deleted as a whole or the individual `Activity` itself was deleted.

fields.name: limited
fields.description:
Information on _whether_ and _how_ this `Activity` has limited spots for participants.

  If This field is `null` this individual `Activity` is _not_ limited
  This can have multiple reasons:
  - This `Activity` is part of an `ActivityGroup` which is limited as a whole, like a _Course_
  - This `Activity` allows for unlimited participants, like e.g. an online class

  If this field is _not_ `null` this `Activity` has a limited number of spots for participants.
  This can be the case for individually bookable `Activities` of e.g. a _Class_ or also for the `Activities` in an `ActivityGroup` like e.g. a _Workshop_ using [Tickets](https://help.eversportsmanager.com/ticket-system-for-workshops-courses-and-events-eversports-help-center).

fields.name: location
fields.description:
The physical location at which this `Activity` will happen.

  Note that e.g. a _Class_ "Yoga in the Park" might happen at a location different from the `Location` of the `Venue`.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
A name for this specific `Activity`.
    Note that not all `Activities` have a specific name. If the name is `null` you can infer its name from the name of the `ActivityGroup`.

    E.g. an `ActivityGroup` called “Morning Yoga” might have `Activities` without specific names, all `Activities` are generic “Morning Yoga” `Activities`.
    But an `ActivityGroup` called “Beginners Course” might contain `Activities` individually named “Week 1 - Basics”, “Week 2 - Breathing”,…

fields.name: start
fields.description: The start of this `Activity` provided in the `DateOutput` format

types.name: DateInput
types.description:
A string representing a point in time in an [ISO Format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)

  When providing a `DateInput` argument you can choose from multiple different formats:
  - `"yyyy-MM-dd"` for just a Date: e.g. `"2022-05-13"` will be interpreted as May 13th 2022, 00:00:00h _UTC_
  - `"yyyy-MM-dd[T]HH:mm"` or `"yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"` for a date with time: e.g. `"2022-05-13 15:30"` will be interpreted as May 13th 2022, 15:30:00h in our _default timezone Europe/Vienna_, which is 14:30 _UTC_
  - `"yyyy-MM-dd[T]HH:mm:ss[Z]"` for a UTC timestamp: e.g. `"2022-05-13T15:30:00Z"` with the Z denoting zero UTC offset will be interpreted as May 13th 2022, 15:30:00h _UTC_
  - `"yyyy-MM-dd[T]HH:mm:ss[±]hh:mm"` for a timestamp with an arbitrary UTC offset: e.g. `"2022-05-13T15:30:00+03:00"` for 15:30 Djibouti time (with a 03:00h UTC offset) will be interpreted as May 13th 2022, 15:30:00h _Djibouti time_, which is 12:30 _UTC_

types.name: DateOutput
types.description:
A string representing a specific point in time in the [ISO Format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) `"yyyy-MM-dd[T]HH:mm:ss[±]hh:mm"` containing the information in which timezone this date is happening.

  For example `"2022-03-15T20:15:00+01:00"` would denote the _15th of March 2022, 20:15:00 local time in a timezone offset by 1 hour from UTC_. (e.g. Vienna)

types.name: PublicationState
types.description:
A status indicating whether an `ActivityGroup` is publicly bookable, visible only, hidden or archived:
- ACTIVE  (This ActivityGroup or the Activities it contains are active and bookable for the public)
- VIEW_ONLY  (This ActivityGroup can not be booked publicly, but is still visible to the public)
- HIDDEN  (This ActivityGroup is set to be hidden from the public. It might be for internal use only, not yet public or hidden after it was cancelled)
- ARCHIVED  (This ActivityGroup is archived. It or its constituent Activities can not be booked.)

args.name: isArchived
args.description:
Filter by whether an `Activity` was _archived_.

  An `Activity` is _archived_ if the `Activity` was deleted or the whole `ActivityGroup` was _deleted_ or _archived_.

  - If `isArchived` is `true` we will only return online archived `Activities`
  - If `isArchived` is `false` we will only return `Activities` that are _not_ archived.

  Default value is `false` to by default exclude archived `Activities`, since they are usually not relevant for integrators.

args.name: isBookableUnit
args.description:
Filter by whether an `Activity` is generally bookable by itself or only as part of an encompassing `ActivityGroup`.

  ### What are Bookable Units?
  An `Activity` is a _bookable unit_ if customers can register for it as single, individual `Activities`.
  For example _Classes_ or _Trainings_.

  An `Activity` is _not_ a _bookable unit_ if it is just the part of a whole bookable `ActivityGroup`, usually containing multiple `Activities`.
  For example _Courses_ or _Workshops_, where customers can only regsiter or buy _tickets_ for the whole `ActivityGroup`, _not_ for individual `Activities`.

  - If `isBookableUnit` is `true` we will only return individually bookable `Activities` and _exclude_ non-bookable unit `Activities`, which are only a part of a larger `ActivityGroup`.
  - If `isBookableUnit` is `false` we will only return non-bookable unit `Activities`, which are part of a larger `ActivityGroup` and _exclude_ individually bookable `Activities` and _exclude_
  - If `isBookableUnit` is not provided we will return both types of `Activities`

args.name: isCancelled
args.description:
Filter by whether an `Activity` was _cancelled_.

  - If `isCancelled` is `true` we will only return online cancelled `Activities`
  - If `isCancelled` is `false` we will only return `Activities` that are _not_ cancelled.
  - If `isCancelled` is not provided we will return both types of `Activities`,

  Since without any `timeRange` filter the results might include `Activities` from many years ago, we recommend that you use this filter.

args.name: isBookableUnit
args.description:
Filter by whether an `ActivityGroup` is generally bookable as a whole or only an organizational unit comprising individually bookable `Activities`.

  ### What are Bookable Units?
  An `ActivityGroup` is a _bookable unit_ if customers can register or buy _tickets_ for the whole `ActivityGroup`.
  For example _Courses_ or _Workshops_.

  An `ActivityGroup` is _not_ a _bookable unit_ if it is just an organizational unit consisting of many individually bookable `Activities`.
  For example _Classes_ or _Trainings_, where customers can only regsiter or each individual `Activity`, but _not_ for the entire `ActivityGroup` as a whole.

  - If `isBookableUnit` is `true` we will only return `ActivityGroups` bookable as a whole and _exclude_ non-bookable unit `ActivityGroups`
  - If `isBookableUnit` is `false` we will only return non-bookable unit `ActivityGroups`, which are organizational units for individually bookable `Activities`
  - If `isBookableUnit` is not provided we will return both types of `ActivityGroups`

args.name: publicationStates
args.description: Filter by the one or more `PublicationStates` of the `ActivityGroup`

args.name: sportIds
args.description:
Filter by the one or more `IDs` of a `Sport`

   You can use this to retrieve only the `ActivityGroups` of one or more specific `Sports`

args.name: teacherIds
args.description:
Filter by the one or more `IDs` of a `Teacher`

    You can use this to retrieve only the `ActivityGroups` taught (at least in part) by one or more specific `Teachers`

    Note that `ActivityGroups` consist of usually more than 1 `Activity`, where each `Activity` can be taught by a different `Teacher`.
    The `ActivityGroups` will match the filter if at least 1 of its _active_(i.e. not cancelled or deleted) `Activities` are taught by one of the provided `Teachers`.

args.name: timeRange
args.description:
Filter by whether an `ActivityGroup` falls (at least partially) within the provided `TimeRange`.

  As an `ActivityGroup` usually consists of multiple `Activities` the `TimeRangeInput` is matched if the _start_ of at least 1 of its constituent `Activities` falls within the given `TimeRange`.
  Note that we only consider _active_ `Activities`, i.e. which are _not_ cancelled or archived.

  Note that both `start` and `end` of this Input are _optional_
  - If `start` is provided we will return all `ActivityGroups` that have at least 1 _active_ `Activity` whose `start` is after or equal to your input.
  - If `end` is provided we will return all `ActivityGroups` that have at least 1 _active_ `Activity` whose `start` is before your input.

  Since without any `timeRange` filter the results might include `ActivityGroups` from many years ago, we recommend that you use this filter.

args.name: types
args.description:
Filter by the one or more `ActivityGroupTypes` of the `ActivityGroup`

    E.g. you could filter to only retrieve _Retreats_ and _Workshops_ by setting `types: [ WORKSHOP, RETREAT ]`

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.
